name: Wairarapa Moana Community Environment Fund
summary: Annual Greater Wellington fund for community and mana whenua restoration projects at Wairarapa Moana (Lakes Wairarapa and Onoke and their wetlands). Grants cover planting, pest control and monitoring.

amount.note: Spendable over up to two years

eligibility.rule: On publicly accessible land, or Māori-owned or private land with evidence of access and wider benefits
Distant mapped-area projects create a positive environmental flow-on effect

calls.label: Annual round (1 August to 1 October)
calls.recurring: Opens 1 August and closes 1 October each year

status.quote: The applications open from 1 August and close on 1 October.

recurring.quote: The applications open from 1 August and close on 1 October.

applicant_types.quote: Mana whenua and community groups can apply for funding to support environmental restoration projects that are:

geography.quote: The project is located within the Wairarapa Moana (see map below).

access.quote: Complete the application form through the Application Portal.

window.quote: The applications open from 1 August and close on 1 October.

amount.quote: Groups can apply for up to $12,500. This money can be spent over up to 2 years.

effort.quote: Complete the Application Form and submit.
Applicant site visits and assessments - first few weeks of October (a representative must be available to do this)

eligibility.quote: On publicly accessible land (e.g., council reserves, Department of Conservation land and some stream margins). There are a couple of exceptions: If the project is on Māori owned land or private land then evidence of access, community participation and wider Wairarapa Moana benefits will need to be provided.
If the project is located within the mapped area but is some distance from the Wairarapa Moana, the restoration activity must contribute to a positive environmental flow on effect
